rubrics.justification: Describes an expanded blastocyst with thinned zona, compact A-grade ICM, and somewhat loose/uneven B-grade TE consistent with 3AB. Minor speculative elements like partial collapse/irregular zona are not clearly verifiable from a single image.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, endometrium, male factor, and first-cycle status well with embryo quality and prognosis. Could more explicitly relate male-factor semen parameters to fertilization/blastulation rather than implantation alone.

Overall logic is clear and internally consistent: good-quality untested Day 5 blastocyst in a favorable young patient yields moderate-good implantation odds. Minor overreach around sperm DNA damage and some repetitive phrasing slightly weaken coherence.

Generally aligned with Gardner grading and standard IVF practice: single embryo transfer, no bed rest, morphology interpreted appropriately, cautious discussion of PGT-A. Slight deviations include somewhat casual endorsement of PGT-A and speculative comments on testicular sperm without stronger indication.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support, review of embryology metrics, and possible sperm DNA fragmentation testing if failure recurs. Useful but not highly detailed on protocol-specific management.
